absent: Numeric values and layouts for device kinds, remap flags, pin bias, LRU enumerations, and statistic identifiers.
Full definitions of hstate, folio, lruvec, batch, cgroup, pagemap, and zone structures beyond fields touched here.
Lock ordering, IRQ, sleep, and context constraints beyond the held assertions and local drain sequencing shown.
Enabling conditions for vmemmap optimization, gigantic modes, evictability, disabled caches, and disabled cgroups.
Retry bounds, error codes, and caller contracts for bulk restore, folio grab, and drain paths beyond success versus failure shown.
Internals of cross-dossier helpers, allocators, flushes, traces, and policy or cpuset queries referenced but not routed here.

findings.text: Bulk restoration walks an input folio collection, restores only entries still marked optimized with TLB flush deferred, counts successes, moves non-optimized entries to an output collection, issues one global flush if any succeeded, and reports either first failure or restored count; a no-optimization build instead transfers the whole input to output and reports success.

Bulk error recovery has two modes. If the secondary collection is non-empty it discards every entry there by clearing huge state and freeing, allowing a later bulk retry. Otherwise it probes input entries one by one, converting failures into surplus list members and, on the first entry that can be restored and freed, stops to allow bulk retry.

Removal from the huge pool detaches the folio from its free list, decrements global and per-node free, surplus-optional, and total counters as applicable, clears the freed marker when present, and clears huge identity only when vmemmap is not optimized; a gigantic no-runtime configuration returns before list or counter updates.
Pool victim selection iterates allowed nodes in free order, skips nodes whose free list is empty and, when reclaiming surplus, nodes without surplus, then removes the first folio found and stops.
Node iteration for freeing is bounded by the weight of the supplied mask and advances through a next-node selector once per step.
Allowed-memory accounting sums per-node free huge counts over the current cpuset, further restricted by an optional bind mask derived from the allocation mask.

Two public uncharge entry points cover normal and reserved huge folio accounting and delegate to a shared helper with a reserved flag; counter selection chooses the reserved or normal per-index counter of the owning cgroup.

The shared huge cgroup uncharge path is inactive when cgroups are disabled or no owner is attached, otherwise detaches the owner, uncharges the selected page counter, releases a subsystem reference for reserved charges, and subtracts pages from per-node usage for normal charges.

Huge pool removal, victim selection, and cgroup uncharge require the huge lock held on entry; bulk error handling additionally takes that lock with IRQ protection around flag clearing and free-list insertion plus a scheduling point after each free.

Zone-device folio release uncharges memory control, handles anonymous accounting and exclusivity clearing, clears a potentially stale mapping except for two device kinds, then dispatches by device kind to driver free plus reference handling, count reset, waiter wakeup, or driver free alone, warning when expected driver state is absent.

LRU insertion first resolves unevictable state and evictability, updating rescue or cull accounting, clearing active and resetting lock count when forced unevictable, then inserts into the vector and emits an insertion trace.

LRU relocation covers tail rotation, generic deactivation, file deactivation, and lazy free. Guards skip unevictable entries, mapped files for file deactivation, inactive entries for generic deactivation, and non-anonymous or cached entries for lazy free. Actions clear active and referenced state, route dirty or writeback files to reclaim marking versus tail rotation, and convert lazy-free candidates by clearing swap backing, with per-class event accounting.

Public deactivation and lazy-free wrappers precheck LRU membership and state, including unevictable, active or reference-generation state for deactivation and anonymous swap-backed non-cached state for lazy free, then queue the folio for the corresponding batched relocation.

Batched LRU movement takes a folio reference, then under a per-CPU batch lock with selectable IRQ protection adds to the current batch and flushes the batch through the supplied action when the batch is full, the folio may not be cached, or caching is disabled.

Batched reference release skips empty slots and the huge zero folio, routes zone-device and huge folios to their dedicated frees after a final reference drop, otherwise cancels deferred split and releases page cache under a single amortized vector lock session, then uncharges and frees only survivors and reinitializes when none survive.

Encoded page release decodes each input to a folio with an optional following multi-reference count, accumulates into fixed batches with intermediate flushes, and drains any remainder; a separate batch release drains per-CPU LRU state once per batch before putting references.

Per-CPU LRU batching and draining serialize with a per-CPU batch lock in IRQ-saving or plain form around add and drain, while batched reference release holds at most one vector lock across consecutive cache releases and drops it before zone-device or huge frees.

Targeted LRU drain for one folio first returns when the folio cannot be cached or its reference count already matches expected plus extra, otherwise performs a local drain and then, if still unmatched, a global drain, recording progress through a caller-provided state.
Global LRU cache disable increments a disable counter, waits for preemption or RCU readers to exit, then drains per-CPU and buffer LRU state on all CPUs or locally on non-SMP builds.

Memory-group reparenting transfers each reclaim list except the unevictable one from child vector to parent vector and moves per-zone LRU sizes rather than copying, so the dying child no longer accounts folios it no longer owns.

Folio grab distinguishes plain get from pin. Pin on a zero folio succeeds without accounting, pin without explicit peer-DMA permission fails on peer-DMA folios, otherwise get adds plain references while pin adds either paired normal plus pin-count references or bias-scaled normal references and records acquisition statistics.

Pin-oriented folio lookup must cope with concurrent split between folio resolution and reference acquisition: after obtaining a putatively stable reference it revalidates that the page still belongs to that folio, dropping the reference and retrying on mismatch, and treats non-positive reference state as failure.

Pin release skips reference changes for the zero folio, records release statistics, reverses either dedicated pin-count plus normal references or bias-scaled normal references depending on folio capability, then drops the computed references.

Pinned-page sanity checking is debug-only, ignores null, zero, and non-anonymous folios, and otherwise expects exclusivity on the head folio for small or huge folios and on either head or constituent page for larger THP mappings, warning on violation.
Single pin release is offered for both page and folio forms; the page form additionally runs pinned-page sanity checking before resolving to a folio and releasing one pin reference.

LRU batching state combines a bounded folio collection with count and drained marker, a global atomic disable counter, per-CPU drain work items, and per-vector reclaim lists linked through folio LRU linkage; a move callback type receives a vector and folio and returns nothing.
Drain orchestration provides a combined local LRU plus buffer plus lock drain, a CPU plus zone variant that also drains local pages, and a per-CPU work handler invoking the combined drain.
